item.title: Clintons tangle with Epstein investigators in deposition videos
item.description: The House Oversight and Government Reform Committee on Monday released video footage of its depositions of Bill and Hillary Clinton, showing the former president and former secretary of State’s responses as they were grilled about their connections to the convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. item.title: Peoria Police: Shooting incidents up, Homicides down
item.description: Shooting incidents in Peoria have increased from 5 in January and February 2025 to 7 in the same period in 2026, while homicides are down 100% and stolen weapons are slightly down.

item.title: Illinois Central College narrows search to 3 presidential finalists
item.description: Illinois Central College has narrowed down its list of candidates for the next institutional president to three, all of whom have proven records of advancing student success, strengthening workforce alignment, driving innovation, and building strategic partnerships.

item.title: Man pleads guilty to 2024 shooting
item.description: Aubrae M. Harper pleaded guilty to Aggravated Battery with a Firearm in connection with a south Peoria shooting, and will be sentenced on April 22.

item.title: Iran tensions could quickly impact gas prices in Central Illinois
item.description: Gas prices in Central Illinois could soon rise due to tensions between the US and Iran, as oil prices have already increased by five percent in response to the conflict.

item.title: Peoria County farmers hope forecasted rain eases drought conditions ahead of planting season
item.description: Farmers in Central Illinois are preparing for planting season, which is just weeks away, and are hoping for rain to help recharge the soil before seeds go into the ground.

item.title: Man dead from carbon monoxide intoxication after Bloomington house fire
item.description: A 40-year-old man, Benjamin L. Duzen, died from carbon monoxide intoxication caused by smoke inhalation from a housefire in Bloomington, Illinois on Sunday.

item.title: Stage two of Bloomington streetscape project construction starts
item.description: The City of Bloomington has begun Stage Two of Phase One of the Downtown Bloomington Streetscape project, which will bring new furnishings, landscaping, street paving, and outdoor dining areas to the 500 block of North Main Street, with ample parking still available in the area.

item.title: Bloomington to cut water loss with upgrades and lead pipe fixes
item.description: The city of Bloomington has been working to reduce water loss since 2019, and with the help of infrastructure improvements and a lead service line program, they believe they are now below 30% water loss.

item.title: New Hope Apartments shutdown is just the beginning warns community service group
item.description: The New Hope Apartments in Peoria, Illinois closed due to federal funding changes, leaving many residents without a home and forcing them to find new places to live.
